title: Preventing Trap Siphonage
description: A drain trap relies on a standing water barrier—the trap seal—to stop harmful sewer gases from entering a building. However, unvented or improperly piped traps, such as unvented S-traps, are highly vulnerable to self-siphonage. When water drains rapidly through the trap, momentum and negative atmospheric pressure can pull the entire water seal down the waste line. Without water remaining at the trap weir, sewer odors flow freely into living spaces. Installing a properly configured P-trap connected to an adequate vent pipe preserves atmospheric balance and keeps the trap seal intact.

Without water remaining at the trap weir, sewer odors flow freely into living spaces. Installing a properly configured P-trap connected to an adequate vent pipe preserves atmospheric balance and keeps the trap seal intact.
